title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's study of the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets) for the elliptic/SL2 level of the Teichmüller tower.
- G is a profinite group modelled on SL(2,Ẑ), the profinite completion of Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6.
- ρ is an element of order 6 and σ an element of order 4, with σ^2 = -1 central.
- ε_0 is a 'parabolic' generator, ε_0 = σρ, the analogue of [[1,1],[0,1]].
- G' is an extension of G by an outer involution τω (from the previous page, τω(ρ) = conjugate of ρ^{-1}).
- B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(G'_{ρ,σ}) × Ẑ^* is the set of pairs (u, μ) such that u sends ρ and σ to conjugates of ρ^μ and σ^μ, and u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ.

Previous page. Since ρ^6 = 1, ρ^μ = ρ^{ε_3(μ)}. Since σ^4 = 1 and σ^{-1} = -σ, σ^μ = ε_2(μ)σ, where ε_2, ε_3 are the characters Ẑ^* → ±1 mod 4 and mod 3.

Proposition (finished on this page). (u, μ) lies in B_{ρ,σ} iff there exist α, β such that:
- (10) u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) and u(σ) = ε_2(μ) int(β)(σ);
- (11) u(ε_0) = ε_0^μ;
- (12) α ∈ G if μ ≡ 1 (3), and α ∈ τ·G otherwise. Conjugation by the outer element realises the inversion of ρ, so ε_3 is absorbed into α.

Reformulation (13)-(14). Put ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = ε_2(μ) β σ(β)^{-1}, where ρ(α) means conjugation of α by ρ. Then u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ. So u is determined by (α, β, μ).

Role of ε_0 (15). If n ↦ ε_0^n from Ẑ to G is injective, then μ is read off from the action of u on the procyclic 'cusp' subgroup L_0 = closure of ⟨ε_0⟩. Hence (u, μ) is determined by u alone, i.e. by (α, β, ε = ε_2(μ)).

When G maps to SL(2,Ẑ) by sending ρ, σ to the usual matrices, the image already determines μ. The next page then says the element is determined by α, β alone.

Next page. Grothendieck turns (11) into a cocycle-type equation of the form ξ σ(y) = ε_0^{μ-1}, and a 2-cycle-type relation y σ(y) = 1. These are the SL2 analogues of the Drinfeld–Ihara GT relations f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 etc. Overall, this is a GT-type description of an automorphism group of a profinite SL2-type group by 'conjugating elements' plus a cyclotomic character.
errors: (12) is heavily struck through and garbled. The intended statement seems to be: α lies in G or in the coset τG according to ε_3(μ) (marginal note 'i.e. α ≡ τ'). As written, the condition is ambiguous.
(13) as transcribed: η = ε_2(μ) β σ(β)^{-1} must be read with σ(β) = σβσ^{-1}, by the same convention as ρ(α). The factor ε_2(μ) is central (±1), so this is consistent.
Grothendieck himself marks the derived relation 'y σ(y) = 1' on the next page as possibly false ('Faux ?').

ideas.what: Describing automorphisms of a profinite SL2(Ẑ)-like group compatible with a cyclotomic character μ: generators of finite order go to conjugates of their μ-powers, and the cusp generator goes exactly to its μ-power. The data are pairs (α, β) of conjugating elements.
ideas.modern_name: GT-type (Grothendieck–Teichmüller) action on profinite SL2(Z) / the Γ_{1,1} level of the Teichmüller tower; 'GT for SL2' / profinite modular group automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; for the genus-one / SL2 level Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto (elliptic GT), Enriquez (elliptic associators)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and its first two levels. The detailed SL2 computation appears to be only in the unpublished 'Longue Marche' notes.

ideas.what: Using injectivity of the cusp map Ẑ → G, n ↦ ε_0^n, to recover the character μ from u alone, via the action on the procyclic parabolic subgroup.
ideas.modern_name: cyclotomic character recovered from inertia at the cusp (faithfulness of the parabolic/inertia subgroup)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings / Esquisse discuss cusps and inertia only in general terms

ideas.what: Absorbing the order-3 / order-4 characters ε_3, ε_2 of μ into conjugation by an outer involution (τω), or into the central sign -1.
ideas.modern_name: normalisation of GT parameters by the extended (anti-holomorphic) modular group GL2 / PGL2(Z)

missed.claim: An explicit, Grothendieck-written parametrisation of the 'GT-type' group B_{ρ,σ} for the genus-one level (SL2 with elliptic elements of orders 4 and 6 and a cusp). Elements are given by data (α, β, μ) subject to an equation obtained from the cusp condition. This prefigures the elliptic GT relations of Lochak–Schneps / Enriquez, carried out in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation.
missed.quote: Pour qu'un (u,μ) ∈ Aut(G'_{ρ,σ}×Ẑ^*) soit dans B_{ρ,σ}, il f.n.s. qu'il existe α…, β∈G tels que … u(ρ)=int(α)(ρ), u(σ)=ε_2(μ) int(β)(σ) … u(ε_0)=ε_0^μ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it documents that Grothendieck worked out SL2-level GT-type equations himself, with the ±1 / ε_2, ε_3 bookkeeping. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially routine setup of a GT-type automorphism group at the SL2 level. It anticipates later work on elliptic GT, but it contains no result beyond what is now known. Its main interest is as a historical record.
transcription_corrections: Line under (12): marginal 'i.e. α ≡ τ' (the 'α' is overwritten), consistent with α lying in the τ-coset when μ ≢ 1 (3).
(13): 'η = ε_2(μ) β σ(β)^{-1}' — the symbol transcribed 'σ[?]' is σ.
Line after (13): likely 'puisqu'on a alors, u par' rather than '[?]'.
'(14) u(ρ) = ξρ' — the transcription 'uφ' is u(ρ).
'le groupe s'envoyant dans Sl(2,Ẑ)' — the phrase is probably 'si G est … muni d'un homomorphisme dans SL(2,Ẑ) …'.
Line 'D'ailleurs, dans le cas où (15) Ẑ → G, n ↦ ε_0^n est injectif, μ est déterminé en fonction de u comme multiplicateur de l'action de u sur L_0 ⊂ G'.
